newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says strategic reviews near completion.
newsitem.headline: BHP says strategic reviews near completion.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Australia's largest listed company, said on Wednesday that it was close to completing its evaluation of assets and its review of business performance.

"The rationalisation of the petroleum group has basically been completed, the steel group strategy review is being implemented, while there are a range of initiatives in copper to improve costs and resource utilisation across that group," managing director John Prescott.
He also said the review of the company's minerals division was expected to be completed over the next few weeks.

"In minerals most effort is being directed at lifting the coal division's performance and at ensuring that the substantial number of new projects are commissioned as effectively as possible," Prescott said.

Prescott said most work in the minerals unit was proceeding in line with expectations except for the previously announced delays at the Hartley platinum mine in Zimbabwe and the Pilbara hot briquetted iron (HBI) project.
"Commissioning of this HBI project is now likely to be later than previously announced with some further cost overruns that have yet to be fully delineated," Prescott said.
Prescott said negotiations were underway with the relevant contractors to define the overuns and these would be announced as soon as possible.
The project remained commercially viable, Prescott said.

Prescott said a team of senior executives involved in the recent asset and business studies in other parts of the company would be assisting minerals officers to complete the review in minerals expected over the next few weeks.
